title: The worst normalization error can require two rays even when every ray looks right
statement: For nonnegative response R and approximation S with positive column masses b_j,d_j, set normalized columns nu_j,nu_tilde_j and r_j=d_j/b_j. The supplied theorem states that any jointly convex posterior discrepancy over c>=0 attains its worst case on at most2 rays, by fixing the TRUE normalization mass-ratio slice before taking a simplex vertex. Single-ray checks can fail: R=I2,S=diag(a,1) agree on each ray but mixture TV reaches(sqrt(a)-1)/(sqrt(a)+1). Scalar target error is exactly optimized pairwise in O(K^2) arithmetic AFTER responses are acquired. With exact masses, uniform coarsening TV equals max_j TV(nu_j,representative_j); scalar interval-cover sorting is optimal. Approximate masses require the two-ray or explicit ratio bound, and all later adaptive queries retain only their original fixed simultaneous acquisition event. Response-cone precision: the two-ray proof fixes the TRUE normalization mass-ratio slice before taking an extremal simplex vertex. It applies to a finitely generated nonnegative CUMULATIVE likelihood cone with acquired masses/response table and earned multiplicative closure; it is not an unrestricted small oracle. Response construction, normalization counterexample, finite-bit/update-algebra/chain costs and ordinary controls remain explicit.

requires: Explicit nonnegative response R[y,j]=E[1{Y=y}ell_j],positive column masses and permitted CUMULATIVE likelihoods sum_j c_j ell_j,c>=0. Multiplicative evidence must stay in the declared cone or require a larger algebra.
Approximate nonnegative response and normalization masses are controlled jointly; checking only conditional distributions at single evidence rays is insufficient.
Adaptive selection inside a fixed simultaneous finite-response guarantee is allowed; new data-dependent dictionaries,nonlocal model edits or changed hypotheses need an earned new guarantee.

costs: After responses are constructed, scalar uniform error is an O(K^2) pairwise optimization; finite-target TV can use O(q log q) sign/root work per pair in exact real arithmetic, with numerical isolation/bit costs separately paid.

Exact-mass scalar coarsening sorts K values in O(K log K); retaining masses/assignments still costs O(K),a dense coefficient query costsOmega(K),and an equally informed exact scalar baseline already supports O(s) changed-coefficient updates.

Dynamic q-state chains readTheta(nq^2) entries,buildO(nq^3),storeO(nq^2),updateO(q^3 log n); a fresh O(nq^2) forward pass can be better for few/broad queries. Gaussian fixed-span reuse is ordinary Woodbury; sparse residual sketches require fixed families and known coercivity.
